# Best rechargeable AA batteries

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro (2550 mAh NiMH).** Digital Camera World's reviewer has used them for years in flash testing and reports total reliability. They are rated to hold about 85% charge after a year and to survive about 500 recharges ([Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)). Their downsides are price and the lower cycle life. The guide's price widget showed about $21.89 for a pack, and it links to Amazon, Adorama, Newegg and Best Buy. I couldn't get a direct product link from the results, so start at that guide page. Prices change, so check at checkout.

**Best for longevity: Panasonic Eneloop (standard, 2000 mAh).** It has lower capacity per charge, but it is rated for about 2,100 recharges and holds 70% charge after 10 years ([Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)). It's a good choice for remotes, mice and devices you charge often.

**Best value: IKEA LADDA.** Charge-Test measured the 2450 mAh version at about 2,450 mAh at low load and 2,348 mAh at 1A, close to Eneloop Pro. It concluded LADDA is Eneloop-class at a lower price ([Charge-Test](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/)).
- The US IKEA page I could see lists the **1900 mAh** version at $9.99 for 4 ([IKEA](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/)).
- I couldn't confirm US pricing or availability for the 2450 mAh pack. One guide quotes $7.99, but the Charge-Test prices are in euros ([GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/)). Check your local IKEA.
- GearLab says Amazon resellers mark LADDA up, which cancels the savings.

**Bulk buy: Tenergy Premium PRO (2800 mAh).** A 20-pack is $42.99, or about $2.15 per cell. It is rated at 1,200 cycles and 85% charge after a year. Smaller packs are 4 for $11.99 and 8 for $21.99 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack)). Those figures are Tenergy's own, not independent tests. The buy link there, [Tenergy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack), is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Returns are within 30 days, and you pay return shipping.

**Devices that need 1.5V:** Digital Camera World recommends the EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA for gear that doesn't work well with 1.2V NiMH cells. It is listed in the same guide ([link](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)).

## Caveats
- **Amazon Basics High-Capacity:** Two Frame & Focal articles say it performs poorly. GearLab instead recommends it for low-drain devices like clocks and remotes. Frame & Focal's numbers are also inconsistent with each other (for example, Eneloop Pro capacity), so I'd treat them cautiously.
- **Chargers:** You'll need a decent charger. IKEA sells the STENKOL for $8.99 ([IKEA](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/)).

**Bottom line:** For high-drain gear like flashes, cameras and controllers, get Eneloop Pro, or LADDA 2450 if you can find it cheaply. For everyday low-drain devices, standard Eneloop or LADDA 1900 is enough.
